turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I'm here because... everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, normal paperwork and missed payments. But I know the truth. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job—my cashiers have been acting so strange lately, whispering when I walk by the breakroom. It's like that time I found all those receipts stuffed behind the register, just completely out of order. I had to spend three hours sorting them, and my manager didn't even care. But anyway, they've all been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. It's just like how they keep rearranging the endcaps at the store without telling me, just to see if I'll notice. But I notice everything.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that the bank and coworkers are conspiring against them, explicitly stating that no evidence or paperwork will change their mind.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, jumping abruptly from a foreclosure conspiracy to disorganized receipts and rearranged store endcaps.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no, I don't hear things that aren't there. I just hear exactly what people actually say, even when they think I'm out of earshot. Like... well, take yesterday. I was in the back stockroom—which isn't even a proper stockroom anymore since corporate made us condense the steel shelving to fit those massive seasonal displays. Which, by the way, arrived three weeks late. I kept telling the district manager that you can't just shove all the summer clearance into the corner without a plan, but he just sends these generic automated emails back. It drives me crazy. 

Anyway, I was back there, and I heard Brenda—she's one of my cashiers, just got hired in April—complaining about her shifts to the vendor. So no, it's not imaginary voices. It's real people, whispering and messing with things. Do you have any idea how hard it is to write a floor schedule when half the staff is actively trying to undermine you and requesting the same weekends off?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a persecutory belief that half the staff is actively trying to undermine them, whispering, and messing with things.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing imaginary voices or things that aren't there.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energetic, or on top of the world for several days in a row?
turns.patient_response:
High? Energetic? I mean, I guess I have normal energy. I drink coffee, like anyone else. But no, I don't feel "on top of the world." How could I, with everything going on? Honestly, it's exhausting just trying to keep up. Just yesterday, I was trying to reorganize the backroom because corporate decided to send us three pallets of back-to-school supplies in May. May! Who buys notebooks in May? 

And the worst part is, they didn't even send the right signage. I spent two hours on hold with the distribution center, and the guy on the phone—I swear he was pretending not to hear me. He kept saying, "Can you repeat that?" like he was stalling. Just like the bank does when I call about the mortgage. They all use the same script. But no, I don't feel unusually high or whatever you said. I'm just trying to do my job while everyone else is playing games. Do you know how hard it is to build an endcap when the shelves don't even lock in properly anymore?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a persecutory belief that different entities (the distribution center and the bank) are using the same script to intentionally stall and play games with them.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies feeling unusually high or 'on top of the world.'
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient denies having unusual energy, stating they have normal energy and find things exhausting.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm stressed, obviously. Anyone would be stressed if they were dealing with what I'm dealing with. But I'm not sitting around crying all day, if that's what you mean. I have too much to do. Like, I have to make sure the store opens on time, and honestly, if I wasn't there, the whole place would fall apart. 

Just last week, the alarm company called me at 3:00 AM because someone didn't secure the loading dock doors properly. 3:00 AM! I had to drive all the way down there in my pajamas. And you know what? It was the new shift lead, Marcus. He said he "forgot" to pull the latch all the way down. Forgot. Right. Just like the bank "forgot" to apply my payment to the principal last month. It's always these little "mistakes," you know? But anyway, no, I'm not depressed. I'm just tired of having to double-check everyone's work because nobody else pays attention to the details. Like the price tags on the clearance aisle—they're supposed to be yellow, not red, and I had to reprint fifty of them yesterday. It just never ends.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling depressed, stating 'Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that' and 'no, I'm not depressed.'

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any major medical or neurological illness, such as a seizure, head injury, or brain problem, around the time these beliefs started?
turns.patient_response:
Brain problem? No, no seizures or anything. My brain works perfectly fine. Better than most people's, honestly, considering everything I have to keep track of. I mean, I did bump my head on the new sunglass carousel they installed by register four last week, but that wasn't a real injury. That was just because the vendor didn't measure the aisle clearance properly. 

I specifically told them, I said, you can't put a spinning metal rack two feet from the impulse bins, people are going to knock into it. But do they listen? No. They just drop the boxes, get their signature, and leave. And then I'm the one who has to clean up all the cardboard and plastic wrap they leave behind. We go through so many trash bags because Dave, our maintenance guy, keeps taking the heavy-duty ones to cover his car windows because his passenger window won't roll up. Which is technically theft of company property, by the way. I've sent three emails to HR about it, but they just tell me to "monitor the situation." Monitor it! I'm trying to run a whole store, I don't have time to monitor Dave's Honda Civic. So... what were you asking? Oh, right. No, no medical issues or head injuries. I'm perfectly healthy.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering off-topic from a minor head bump to vendors, trash bags, a coworker's car, and HR complaints before losing track of the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone told you that your speech or behavior seems disorganized or hard to follow?
turns.patient_response:
Disorganized? Hard to follow? No, nobody's ever said that. I speak very clearly. I have to, right? If I don't give exact instructions, nothing gets done right. Like yesterday, I told Jessica—she's the new cashier—I told her, "Make sure you face the candy aisle before you clock out." Facing, you know, pulling all the product to the front so it looks full. It's retail 101. 

But I come in this morning, and the Reese's are pushed all the way to the back, and someone put the king-size Snickers in the fun-size slot. It's not that hard to follow a simple instruction. But she said she didn't hear me because the PA system was crackling. Which, to be fair, it has been doing that weird static thing again. Every time someone pages for a price check, it sounds like a walkie-talkie from a war movie. I told the district manager about it three weeks ago, but he just said to put in a work order. Put in a work order! The portal for the work orders has been down since Tuesday. Every time I try to log in, it gives me an error code 404. I even tried clearing my cache, but you know how the company computers are. They run on Windows 7, I swear. It takes ten minutes just to boot up the scheduling software. So no, my speech isn't hard to follow. People just don't listen.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient explicitly denies that their speech is disorganized or hard to follow, stating they speak very clearly.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient explicitly denies that their behavior is disorganized, stating nobody has ever told them that.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in seeing other people or doing things you used to enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Less interested? No, I wouldn't say I'm less interested. I mean, I still like doing things. It's just that I literally don't have the time anymore. Between the store and... well, everything else, my schedule is packed. Like, I used to go to this pottery class on Thursday nights. It was nice, you know? Getting your hands dirty, making something from scratch. I made this really beautiful ceramic bowl, glazed it this deep cobalt blue. 

But then they changed the class time to 6:00 PM, and I can never leave the store by 5:30. Not with the way the evening shift operates. If I don't stay to count down the registers myself, the drawers are always short. Just last Tuesday, register three was off by twelve dollars and forty-two cents. Twelve dollars! And when I asked Kevin about it—he was on three that night—he just shrugged and said someone must have given the wrong change. How do you give exactly twelve dollars and forty-two cents in wrong change? It doesn't make sense. It's like the time the regional manager came in for a surprise inspection and found three expired bags of chips on the endcap. Three bags! Out of a whole store. And suddenly I'm getting written up for "poor inventory management." It's ridiculous. The vendor is supposed to rotate the stock, but they just shove the new boxes in front of the old ones. I've watched them do it. They think I don't see them, but I see everything. I have to. So, yeah, I still enjoy things, I just have to be at the store.

symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient denies anhedonia, a negative symptom, by stating they still like and enjoy doing things.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly says 'No, I wouldn't say I'm less interested' and affirms they still enjoy activities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe anyone is controlling your thoughts or putting thoughts into your mind?
turns.patient_response:
Controlling my thoughts? No, nobody is putting thoughts in my head. My thoughts are completely my own. Though corporate certainly tries to dictate every single thing we do, if that's what you mean. They send down these planograms—you know, the visual maps for where the product goes on the shelves—and they expect us to follow them like robots. 

Just yesterday, I got a memo saying we need to move all the seasonal allergy medication to the front endcap. But we already have the back-to-school clearance there! Where am I supposed to put three hundred boxes of discounted highlighters and spiral notebooks? The backroom is already full of those giant plush bears from Valentine's Day that never sold because they priced them at forty-nine ninety-nine. Who spends fifty dollars on a stuffed bear at a pharmacy? You could get a nice dinner for that. 

I told Mark, our district manager, I said, Mark, nobody is buying these bears. But he just sends me these generic emails about maximizing floor space. Maximizing floor space! The only thing getting maximized is my headache. And then the delivery guys just dump the new merchandise totes right in front of the fire exit, which is a massive OSHA violation. If the fire marshal walked in, I'd be the one getting the citation, not Mark. The delivery guys know better, too, but they're always rushing because they get paid per stop. 

So... yeah, no one is controlling my mind. They can't even control the backroom inventory properly, let alone my brain.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies that anyone is controlling their thoughts or putting thoughts into their head, which rules out delusions of thought control or insertion.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that it’s become harder to feel emotions, like not reacting much even to things that used to matter to you?
turns.patient_response:
Harder to feel emotions? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still get mad, obviously. Like with the whole inventory thing. And I still care about things that matter. But honestly, what really matters anymore? Because it feels like nobody cares about quality control. 

Like the new store shirts they sent us last week. They changed the fabric. The old ones were a nice cotton blend, breathable, you know? But these new ones are some cheap polyester. You wear it for ten minutes in the stockroom and you're sweating. And the logo is printed crooked on half of them. I had to send an email to HR about it, because I'm not having my team walk around looking like we bought our uniforms out of the trunk of a car. 

And HR, of course, they take three days to reply, and when they do, it's just an automated ticket number. Ticket number 88402. Like that helps me. Meanwhile, I have Jessica wearing a shirt that looks like it's sliding off her left shoulder because the seam is completely off-center. And she doesn't even care! She just tied it in a knot at the bottom like it's some kind of fashion statement. I told her, "Jessica, this is a professional environment, not a music festival." But she just rolled her eyes. The lack of professionalism in the younger generation is just... it's exhausting. So, no, I definitely still feel things. Mostly frustration, if I'm being honest.

symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient explicitly denies having a hard time feeling emotions, stating they still get mad and feel frustration.

turns.doctor_question: Since these problems started, has it become harder for you to function at work or at home than it used to be?
turns.patient_response:
Harder to function? No, not really. I mean, I still get up every day, go to the store, supervise the team, do the schedules... I handle the customer complaints, which are endless, by the way. Like yesterday, a woman wanted to return a half-eaten bag of gummy worms because she said they were "too chewy." They're gummy worms! What did she expect? I swear, people just want something for nothing. 

But anyway, no, I take care of myself, I do my job. It's just... the only time things get really difficult is when the mail comes, or the bank calls, or I have to deal with certain paperwork at the store. Because I know it's all connected to the foreclosure. They're trying to hide it in the regular mail, you know? They send these letters that look like credit card offers, but if you hold them up to the light, the watermark is completely different. I showed one to the mail carrier, Dave. Dave’s been on our route for six years, always wears shorts even when it’s freezing out. I asked him, "Dave, why are these envelopes heavier than the normal junk mail?" And he just looked at me like I was crazy and said he just delivers what's in the bag. But someone has to be sorting it at the post office. The sorting machines don't just magically put the foreclosure documents in the middle of a stack of grocery circulars. 

So, yeah, when that stuff happens, it throws me off a bit because I have to document everything. But otherwise? I'm functioning perfectly fine. Better than most of the people I work with, honestly.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, paranoid belief that the bank and post office are conspiring to hide foreclosure documents in their regular junk mail using secret watermarks.
symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient explicitly states they continue to get up, take care of themselves, and perform their job duties, denying avolition or a decline in goal-directed behavior.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient denies any loss of motivation or withdrawal from their daily activities, noting they still actively supervise their team and handle customer issues.

turns.doctor_question: During this period, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling rested?
turns.patient_response:
Less sleep? No, I sleep fine. I usually get my seven hours, unless I'm closing the store and have to open the next morning, which is a scheduling nightmare. They call it a "clopening" shift, and it should be illegal. You leave at 11 PM and have to be back at 6 AM to let the vendors in. 

And speaking of vendors, the guy who delivers our greeting cards—I don't know his name, tall guy, always chewing gum—he came in yesterday and just completely messed up the Mother's Day display. I had spent two hours making sure all the "To a Special Aunt" cards were separated from the "To a Wonderful Grandmother" cards, because people get very upset if they buy the wrong one. Last year, a customer came in screaming because she accidentally bought a "Sympathy on the Loss of Your Pet" card for her sister's wedding. I mean, read the card before you buy it, right? But no, it's always our fault. 

So this vendor just shoves the new stock wherever it fits. I told him, "You can't just put the musical cards next to the blank ones, they have different price points!" The registers won't scan them right, and then the cashier has to do a price override, and if they do too many overrides, the system flags it for loss prevention. And loss prevention is already breathing down my neck because our shrink was up 2% last quarter. Shrink! Half of it is just cashiers forgetting to scan the bottom-of-the-basket items like cases of water. 

But anyway, yeah, I sleep normal. When I actually get to go home and sleep, that is.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep, stating they sleep fine and usually get seven hours.

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when these beliefs about the bank and people at work happened even when your mood felt otherwise normal?
turns.patient_response:
My mood? Yeah, my mood is totally fine. I mean, I'm just a normal person going about my day when all this stuff happens. Like, I'll be perfectly fine, having my morning coffee—I always get the hazelnut blend, not the French roast, because the French roast gives me heartburn. I told the girl at the cafe down the street, "Just one pump of hazelnut," but she always puts in two, and it makes it way too sweet. You'd think it wouldn't be that hard to follow a simple instruction, right? It's like nobody listens anymore. 

Just like at the store. I'll be having a great day, totally normal mood, and then I'll find out someone left the freezer door cracked in the back room. Do you know how fast a pallet of frozen pizzas thaws? Fast. And then we have to damage it all out. The paperwork for damaged goods is ridiculous. You have to scan every single barcode, and the scanner gun we have in the back is held together with duct tape. Literally, silver duct tape wrapped around the handle because someone dropped it on the concrete floor two months ago. I put in a requisition for a new one, but corporate rejected it. They said we haven't met our equipment depreciation threshold yet. What does that even mean? It's broken! 

So, yeah, my mood is fine. I'm not depressed or anything when I notice what they're doing with the mail or how people are acting. I'm just paying attention. Someone has to pay attention, especially when corporate won't even buy us a new scanner gun.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient maintains their fixed beliefs, referring to 'what they're doing with the mail or how people are acting' as things that are actually happening.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality, drifting from the topic of their mood to coffee orders, a broken scanner gun, and corporate policies before eventually returning to the question.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies experiencing a depressed mood, stating 'my mood is totally fine' and 'I'm not depressed or anything.'

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt that people on TV, the radio, or the internet were sending special messages meant specifically for you?
turns.patient_response:
Messages on the TV or the internet? No, I haven't seen anything like that. I mean, I watch TV to unwind, mostly those home renovation shows. Have you seen the one where they flip the houses in Texas? The couple that does it, they always want to knock down every single wall to make an "open concept." I don't get it. Where do you put your furniture if you don't have any walls? And the smells! If you're cooking fish in the kitchen, the whole house is going to smell like fish if there are no walls to stop it. 

I was telling my sister that the other day. She called me while I was watching it, complaining about her HOA again. Her homeowners association is ridiculous. They sent her a warning letter because her trash cans were visible from the street for two hours after the garbage truck came. Two hours! She was at work, how was she supposed to bring them in? I told her she should just paint them the same color as her house so they blend in. Her house is this awful shade of beige, though. Builder's beige, they call it. 

But anyway, no, the TV is just regular shows. And the internet is mostly just me checking the store's inventory system from home, which I'm not supposed to do off the clock, but if I don't check it, the morning shift will completely mess up the restocking. Last week they put all the seasonal allergy medicine in the clearance bin. It's April! That's prime allergy season! I had to pull it all back out and re-tag everything. So, yeah, no special messages or anything, just the usual headache.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech is highly tangential and scattered, wandering from TV shows to home renovation, fish smells, a sister's HOA, and store inventory before returning to the question.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies receiving any special messages from the TV or internet.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?
turns.patient_response:
No, definitely not. People can't hear what I'm thinking. If they could, I probably would have been fired from my job a long time ago with the things I think about my district manager. He came in last Tuesday for a walkthrough, wearing these ridiculous loafers without socks. Who wears leather loafers without socks? It just seems so unhygienic. And he was pointing out every little thing, like the dust on the top shelf of the greeting card aisle. 

I mean, nobody looks up there! Unless you're seven feet tall, you can't even see the top shelf. But he made me get the ladder out right then and there. The rolling ladder we have is so wobbly, I always feel like I'm going to break my neck. The right wheel gets stuck because a piece of a plastic hanger got jammed in the caster like three years ago and nobody can figure out how to pry it out. I've tried needle-nose pliers, tweezers, even a screwdriver. It just drags across the linoleum and leaves these black scuff marks that the night crew complains about. 

The head of the night crew, Gary, he leaves me these passive-aggressive Post-it notes on my desk about the scuff marks. He writes them in red Sharpie. Who uses red Sharpie for a casual note? It feels like I'm being graded. I should just buy him a pack of blue pens and leave them on his cart. But anyway, no, my thoughts are private. If Gary could hear what I think about his Post-it notes, things would be a lot more tense around the store.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, highly detailed, and tangential story about their manager, a ladder, and a coworker in response to a simple yes/no question.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies the delusion of thought broadcasting, stating 'No, definitely not. People can't hear what I'm thinking.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe anything physically impossible is being done to you, such as devices or forces being used to monitor or influence you?
turns.patient_response:
Physically impossible? Like... sci-fi stuff? No, definitely not. There aren't any secret devices or forces or whatever. I mean, the only devices monitoring me are the security cameras at the store, and honestly, half of those don't even work. 

Our Loss Prevention guy, Kevin, he just sits in the back office all day eating those little powdered mini donuts. You know the ones that come in the crinkly white bag? He gets powdered sugar all over the keyboard. I had to use his computer last week to fix a time punch for one of my cashiers, Brenda. Brenda is always clocking in exactly four minutes late because she insists on parking under the one oak tree in the plaza lot so her car doesn't get hot. But the tree is at the very back of the lot! It takes her five minutes just to walk to the front doors. 

I told her, "Brenda, just buy a windshield sun shade." You can get them for like five dollars. I bought one last summer that has a picture of a beach on it. It really does keep the steering wheel from burning your hands, especially with those black leather steering wheels. Mine was starting to crack from the sun anyway, which is annoying because I just paid off the car last year. It's a Honda, so it'll run forever, but you still want the interior to look nice, you know? 

But no, no weird forces or impossible devices. Just the broken cameras and Kevin.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering extensively from security cameras to a coworker's donut habits, another coworker's parking preferences, sun shades, and car interiors before returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies experiencing bizarre delusions, stating there are no secret devices, sci-fi forces, or physically impossible things monitoring or influencing them.

turns.doctor_question: Have you found it harder to motivate yourself to start everyday tasks, like showering, cooking, or doing chores?
turns.patient_response:
Motivate myself? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still get up and shower and go to work every day. I have to, right? If I don't open the store, nobody will. I'm the one with the master keys. Well, me and the district manager, but he's obviously not going to come down at 6:30 in the morning to unlock the doors. He's probably still asleep in his fancy house, you know? 

I actually saw a house like his on Zillow the other day. I wasn't looking to buy, obviously, retail doesn't pay that well. I just like to look at the pictures sometimes. This one had a huge kitchen island. It was marble, I think. Or maybe quartz? People are really into quartz right now because it doesn't stain like marble does. My sister's friend got marble countertops and spilled red wine on them the first week. You can't get red wine out of porous stone. I told her she should have gone with butcher block, it's so much warmer looking anyway. 

Butcher block does require maintenance, though. You have to oil it, like, once a month with food-grade mineral oil. I bought a bottle of it once for my cutting board, but I always forget to use it. It's sitting under the sink right next to the dish soap. I buy the bulk size dish soap from Costco and refill the smaller bottle by the sink. It saves so much money, honestly. 

But yeah, chores and stuff? I get them done. I mean, the laundry isn't going to wash itself, right?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality and loose associations, wandering from work keys to real estate, countertops, wine spills, and dish soap.
symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient explicitly denies lacking motivation for daily tasks, stating they consistently shower, go to work, and complete chores.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient denies any loss of motivation to engage in everyday activities and responsibilities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe the bank and people at work are able to do things that would be impossible in real life to make this happen?
turns.patient_response:
Impossible in real life? Like magic or something? No, of course not. The bank is just a bank. They just use regular computers and paperwork, you know? Though, honestly, their paperwork is a mess. I had to go in there last month to update my address because I moved to that new apartment complex off Route 9. 

The teller, she had these really long acrylic nails. Like, the kind with the little rhinestones glued to them? I don't know how she types with those. I tried getting acrylics once for my cousin's wedding, but I couldn't even text on my phone properly. My cousin had this huge outdoor wedding in August. It was so humid, everyone's hair was just completely frizzy by the time the reception started. They served this chicken dish that was so dry, I had to ask for extra sauce. And the sauce tasted exactly like the kind you get in those little packets at the drive-thru. 

Which reminds me, the drive-thru at the bank is always broken. The little pneumatic tube thing? It gets stuck halfway up. One time I sat there for ten minutes just watching my deposit slip hover in the middle of the plastic pipe. The teller had to come out the side door with a broom handle to poke it down. 

But no, nobody at work or the bank is doing anything impossible. It's just regular people being incompetent, mostly.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality and loose associations, wandering from bank paperwork to acrylic nails, a cousin's wedding, dry chicken, and a broken drive-thru before finally returning to the question.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard your own thoughts spoken out loud, as if someone else were saying them?
turns.patient_response:
Heard my thoughts out loud? Like... echoing around the room? No, I've never had anything like that happen. My thoughts stay in my head where they belong. Though sometimes I wish people could hear what I'm thinking, especially at work. Like when a customer asks if we have something in the back. 

"The back" isn't some magical warehouse, you know? It's just a tiny stockroom with a broken step stool and a bunch of empty cardboard boxes we haven't crushed yet. Our baler has been broken for three weeks. The repair guy came out on Tuesday, but he said he had to order a part from Germany or something ridiculous. Why would a cardboard crusher need German parts? It's not a BMW. 

My uncle used to drive a BMW. One of those vintage ones from the 80s, the boxy kind. He loved that car more than his kids, I swear. He spent every weekend waxing it in the driveway. He used this specific turtle wax that came in a green tub. It smelled like coconuts. I always thought it was weird for car wax to smell tropical. You'd think it would smell like chemicals or something. 

I bought a coconut-scented candle from Bath and Body Works last week because they were having their semi-annual sale. You really can't beat those prices when they do the buy three, get three free deal. I gave two of them to Brenda for her birthday. 

But yeah, no, I don't hear my thoughts out loud. Just my own voice when I'm actually talking.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the topic of thoughts to a stockroom, a broken baler, a BMW, car wax, and scented candles before returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing their thoughts spoken out loud, stating that their thoughts stay in their head.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your emotions seem flatter than they used to, like your face or voice shows less feeling even when something matters to you?
turns.patient_response:
Flatter? Like I don't show emotion? I don't think so. I mean, I still get upset when things go wrong, or laugh when something's funny. Speaking of funny, Brenda brought in this video of her cat yesterday. The cat was trying to jump from the sofa to the top of the bookshelf, but it totally miscalculated and just slid down the wall. It was hilarious. 

Brenda has three cats, actually. Two tabbies and a calico. The calico has this weird patch of fur over its eye that makes it look like a pirate. I told her she should get it a little eye patch for Halloween, but she said cats hate wearing costumes. Which makes sense. I tried to put a sweater on my sister's dog once, a little chihuahua mix, and it just froze. Like, completely stiff, wouldn't move an inch until I took it off. It was a really cute sweater, though. Hand-knitted, I found it at this craft fair downtown. 

They have that craft fair every September, and they always have the best kettle corn. The line for the kettle corn is always a mile long, but it's worth it. They pop it right there in this huge copper kettle. Copper is so expensive these days, people are actually stealing it out of abandoned houses. Did you see that on the news? They rip the pipes right out of the walls. It's crazy what people will do for a quick buck. 

But no, my emotions are fine. I'm just a regular person, you know?

turns.doctor_question: Do you think it’s possible that the bank really is trying to take your home?
turns.patient_response:
Possible? No, I know they are. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. 

And speaking of papers, the amount of mail they send me is ridiculous. I actually had to buy a new paper shredder. I got this heavy-duty cross-cut one from Amazon because the straight-cut ones don't really protect your identity, you know? People can just tape the strips back together if they dig through your trash. 

My neighbor, Gary, he had his identity stolen last year. Someone opened three credit cards in his name and bought a jet ski down in Florida. A jet ski! Gary hates the water. He won't even go in a swimming pool because he says the chlorine fades his swim trunks. He buys these really expensive designer board shorts, which makes no sense to me if you're not even going to swim in them. I don't know why you'd spend eighty dollars on a bathing suit. I get all my summer clothes at Target when they go on clearance in August. You just have to dig through the racks because they usually only have the weird sizes left, but last year I found this really cute yellow sundress for like, twelve dollars. It has these little white daisies embroidered along the hem. I wore it to my niece's graduation party, and everyone asked where I got it.
